meta.location: Mulek, Bountiful, and the borders by the west sea
principles: Prisoners set to build their own prison

world_behind.title: The prisoners bury the dead first
world_behind.text: Verse 1 has them compelled to bury both armies' dead under guard. The chapter opens on the work of clearing a battlefield.

world_behind.title: Lehi is described as another Moroni
world_behind.text: Verse 2 says he had been with Moroni in most of his battles, was a man like him, and that they were beloved by each other.

world_behind.title: The Bountiful works are built by Lamanites
world_behind.text: Verses 3 through 5 have the prisoners dig a ditch, raise a breastwork of timbers, and pile the earth against it, then be held inside the wall they made.

world_behind.title: Mormon gives the reason as manpower
world_behind.text: Verse 5 says the labor made them easy to guard, and that Moroni wanted all his forces free for an attack.

world_behind.title: Losses in the west are blamed on Nephite dissension
world_behind.text: Verses 8 and 9 say intrigue among themselves cost a number of cities while Moroni was away.

world_behind.title: The people of Ammon nearly break their oath
world_behind.text: Verses 13 and 14 have them moved with compassion and about to take up arms, and Helaman's persuasion stops them.

world_behind.title: The sons never entered the covenant
world_behind.text: Verse 16 says they had not taken it, so they assemble, call themselves Nephites, and covenant to fight. Two thousand of them.

words.text: A low defensive wall raised for cover. The word occurs three times in this record and never in the King James Bible; Mosiah 11 has Noah building one for a tower. Here it is timbers on the inner bank of a ditch, with the excavated earth piled against it.
Underhand scheming. The word occurs twice in this record and never in the King James Bible, both in this chapter. Mormon names it as the reason Moroni was absent and cities were lost.
Fellow-feeling that moves to act. The people of Ammon are moved with it when they see what the Nephites bear for them, and it nearly costs them the oath of Alma 24.

Brave, stout in battle. The record uses it three times and the King James Bible thirty-two, usually of named warriors. Mormon applies it to two thousand unnamed young men and then adds three more qualities.

Physical vigor and readiness. The word occurs once in this record and once in the King James Bible, where Pharaoh asks Joseph whether any of his brethren are men of activity. Mormon lists it with courage and strength.

A youth, not yet a grown man. The word occurs twice in this record and once in the King James Bible, where Saul asks whose son the stripling David is. Mormon uses it of the two thousand at the moment they march.

phrases.term: Did compel them to go forth and bury their dead
phrases.text: The first labor imposed on the prisoners. Mormon notes they buried Nephite dead as well, which makes the work a service and a punishment at once.

phrases.term: He was a man like unto Moroni, and they rejoiced in each other's safety
phrases.text: Mormon's portrait of Lehi in one line. The comparison to Moroni is the highest praise the record has been using, and he adds that they were beloved by each other.

phrases.term: Within a wall which they had caused them to build with their own hands
phrases.text: The prisoners are kept inside their own work. Mormon states the irony plainly and then gives the practical reason in the same verse.

phrases.term: Because it was easy to guard them while at their labor
phrases.text: The policy explained as arithmetic. Working prisoners need fewer guards, and Moroni wanted his forces available. Mormon supplies the reasoning rather than leaving it to be admired.

phrases.term: Because of iniquity amongst themselves, yea, because of dissensions and intrigue
phrases.text: Mormon assigns the western losses to internal politics. The sentence repeats the cause twice, and it is the same diagnosis Alma 51 gave for the eastern cities.

phrases.term: According to their oath they would have perished
phrases.text: Mormon states what keeping the covenant would actually have cost. The people of Ammon would have died rather than fight, and only the pity of Ammon and his brethren prevented it.

phrases.term: They were moved with compassion and were desirous to take up arms
phrases.text: The pressure on the oath comes from love rather than from fear. They watch what the Nephites suffer on their behalf and want to help, which is the hardest form of the temptation.

phrases.term: Helaman feared lest by so doing they should lose their souls
phrases.text: The reason given for stopping them. Helaman treats the covenant as binding regardless of the circumstances, and the cost is that the people of Ammon must watch.

phrases.term: They had many sons, who had not entered into a covenant
phrases.text: The solution turns on a technicality that Mormon states as a simple fact. The oath bound those who made it and nobody else.

phrases.term: They were true at all times in whatsoever thing they were entrusted
phrases.text: Mormon's summary of the two thousand, and he marks it as the important one. Courage, strength, and activity come first; this is what he says was not all.

phrases.term: Helaman did march at the head of his two thousand stripling soldiers
phrases.text: The march that opens Alma 56 through 58. Mormon gives it in one verse here and returns to it three chapters later in Helaman's own words.

verses.label: v. 1–2
verses.title: After the battle
verses.text: Guards are set over the prisoners, who are made to bury the dead of both armies. Moroni gives Mulek to Lehi, a man who had been with him through most of his battles, like him, and beloved by him and by the people.

verses.label: v. 3–5
verses.title: The wall at Bountiful
verses.text: The prisoners are marched to Bountiful and set to dig a ditch, build a breastwork of timbers on its inner bank, and cast the earth against it. The city becomes a stronghold, and they are held inside the wall they built, because laboring prisoners are easier to guard.

verses.label: v. 6–7
verses.title: The account so far
verses.text: Moroni has beaten one of the greatest Lamanite armies, taken Mulek, and built a prison. He attempts no more battles that year, employing his men in fortifying, feeding the armies, and delivering women and children from famine.

verses.label: v. 8–9
verses.title: The western losses
verses.text: In Moroni's absence, and because of intrigue and dissension among the Nephites, the Lamanites gain ground on the west sea and take a number of cities. Mormon says the internal quarrels put them in the most dangerous circumstances.

verses.label: v. 10–15
verses.title: The oath tested
verses.text: The people of Ammon, converted Lamanites protected by the Nephites, are kept from arms by their oath and would have perished by it. Seeing what the Nephites bear for them, they are moved to fight. Helaman persuades them not to break the covenant, fearing for their souls, so they watch instead.

verses.label: v. 16–19
verses.title: The sons
verses.text: Their sons had never entered the covenant. As many as could bear arms assemble, call themselves Nephites, and covenant to fight for Nephite liberty and never to give it up. Two thousand of them, and they want Helaman to lead them.

verses.label: v. 20–23
verses.title: What they were
verses.text: Young, valiant for courage, strength, and activity, and true at all times in whatever they were trusted with. Men of truth and soberness, taught to keep the commandments and walk uprightly. Helaman marches at their head to the southern border by the west sea.

chapter.title: The prisoners build the fortress that holds them
chapter.text: Mormon states it directly in verse 5 and then explains the logistics. The image and the reasoning are given together.

chapter.title: Labor is used because guards are scarce
chapter.text: The policy is presented as a manpower calculation rather than as cruelty or cleverness. Moroni wanted his whole force free.

chapter.title: Internal politics cost more ground than battles
chapter.text: Verses 8 and 9 attribute a string of lost cities to intrigue at home. Alma 51 said the same about the east; Mormon is building a pattern.

chapter.title: The oath is treated as binding under any pressure
chapter.text: Helaman does not weigh the emergency against the covenant. His stated fear is for their souls, and the people of Ammon are left to watch.

chapter.title: The record admits what the covenant would have cost
chapter.text: Verse 11 says they would have perished by it. Mormon does not soften the arithmetic of a promise kept.

chapter.title: The sons are eligible because nobody bound them
chapter.text: No argument is made about whether the oath should extend. Mormon states the fact and the two thousand assemble.

chapter.title: They name themselves
chapter.text: Verse 16 says they called themselves Nephites. A group of Lamanite descent takes the name of the people they are defending.

chapter.title: Trustworthiness is ranked above courage
chapter.text: Mormon lists valor, strength, and activity, then says this was not all, and gives being true at all times as the thing that mattered.

applications.title: Give the work to the people you are watching
applications.text: Moroni set prisoners to labor because it took fewer guards. Where you are spending effort supervising, consider whether the task itself could do the supervising.

applications.title: Watch for the pressure that comes from love
applications.text: The people of Ammon nearly broke their oath out of compassion. The hardest challenges to a commitment usually arrive as a good reason rather than a temptation.

applications.title: Keep the promise when keeping it is costly
applications.text: Mormon says plainly they would have perished by it. Before you make a commitment, consider what it would look like to keep it on the worst day.

applications.title: Be the one who is true at all times
applications.text: Mormon ranked reliability above courage in two thousand soldiers. Decide to be someone whose word holds in the small things nobody is checking.

questions.text: Who is the person whose safety I rejoice in?
What am I guarding that would guard itself if it had work to do?
What internal quarrel of mine is costing more than any outside pressure?
What good reason is currently pressing me to break something I promised?
Have I ever had to watch while others bore what I could not help with?
What am I free to do that others around me are not?
Am I true in the things I have been entrusted with when nobody checks?

entries.head: Alma 24:18

anchor.quote: they had taken an oath that they never would shed blood more

entries.reason: the covenant itself, made over buried weapons

targets.quote: they never would use weapons again for the shedding of man's blood;
targets.verse_text: And this they did, it being in their view a testimony to God, and also to men, that they never would use weapons again for the shedding of man's blood; and this they did, vouching and covenanting with God, that rather than shed the blood of their brethren they would give up their own lives; and rather than take away from a brother they would give unto him; and rather than spend their days in idleness they would labor abundantly with their hands.
targets.markdown: And this they did, it being in their view a testimony to God, and also to men, that **they never would use weapons again for the shedding of man's blood**; and this they did, vouching and covenanting with God, that rather than shed the blood of their brethren they would give up their own lives; and rather than take away from a brother they would give unto him; and rather than spend their days in idleness they would labor abundantly with their hands.
